Open Days / Personal Visits
See happiness in action
At St Andrew’s Prep, we believe the best way to understand life at our school is to see it in action on a typical school day. That’s why we don’t hold traditional or general open days. Every family is different, and we know a fixed event isn’t always the most convenient or meaningful way to experience a school.
Instead, we create a personalised visit tailored around you, your child and what matters most to your family. Whether you’d like an informal chat over coffee, a private meeting with our Headmaster and a guided tour of the school, or a no-obligation taster experience for your child lasting anywhere from one to three days, we’ll tailor the experience to give you a genuine feel for life at St Andrew’s Prep and the confidence to decide whether it’s the right school for your family.
Whether you’d like an informal conversation or you’re ready to arrange a personalised visit or taster experience Catherina Ashford, Registrar, will be delighted to help. Simply get in touch to discuss what would work best for you and your family, email: cashford@standrewsprep.co.uk or call +44 (0) 1323 74484.
Where Next?
Latest News
What our parents say
Admissions Welcome

Seniors Performance of Oliver Jr.
There is always something rather special about a St Andrew’s Prep production and this year’s Senior performance of Oliver! was no exception. From first note to final curtain, it was a confident showcase of talent and the genuine joy our cast brings to the stage.
Every pupil had a vital role in the success of the show. Whether it was standout moments centre stage, bringing depth as part of the chorus or working tirelessly behind the scenes, there was a true sense of community carried through every scene.
Across multiple performances from 9 to 11 June, the energy never dimmed. Pupils supported one another whilst embracing the butterflies and pouring everything into the performance. The production was enjoyed by the entire school community, as well as parents, staff and visiting schools.
Headmaster, Tom Gregory, said:
“It was an absolute joy from start to finish, a production that will live long in the memory. Bumble, Fagin, Nancy, Dodger, Bill and Oliver are some of the most iconic characters in musical theatre, and our pupils brought them to life with such confidence, character and charm that any West End stage would have welcomed them.”
The pupils worked incredibly hard throughout rehearsals to bring this show to life. We are immensely proud of every pupil who contributed and deeply grateful to the staff whose dedication brought this vision to life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating Creativity: Masterpieces Art Exhibition and Auction Opens
pageCache.text:
Celebrating Creativity: Masterpieces Art Exhibition and Auction Opens
The Masterpieces Art Exhibition and Auction is now open, inviting the Eastbourne community to explore and bid on an inspiring collection of artwork while supporting the Blue Sky Bursaries Appeal. Bringing together work from pupils at St Andrew’s Prep and Eastbourne College alongside contributions from local artists and supporters, the exhibition celebrates creativity in all its forms. From colourful early-years artwork to accomplished paintings, textiles and photography, the collection showcases the imagination, talent and artistic development of young people across our schools.
The exhibition also features a diverse range of works donated by professional artists and members of the local creative community. Highlights include a limited-edition print by renowned artist Robert Tavener, generously donated by Emma Mason Prints, alongside pieces by local photographer Matt Garcia, artist and tattooist Jessica Langstreth, landscape artist Marcus Cherrill, portrait artist Lindy Dunbar, Alex Vanotti and Fi Nolan. With bidding starting from just £5, the auction offers something for everyone – whether you’re looking for an affordable piece of original artwork, a unique gift or a special addition to your collection. The exhibition is on display in the Birley Centre at Eastbourne College and can be viewed in person by appointment. Visitors are warmly encouraged to explore the collection first-hand and discover the breadth of talent on display.
For those unable to visit in person, the full catalogue and online auction can be viewed online. View the auction and place a bid: www.jumblebee.co.uk/bsbmasterpieces2026 All proceeds from the auction will support the Blue Sky Bursaries Appeal, helping to open up opportunities for talented young people to benefit from an education at St Andrew’s Prep and Eastbourne. The Masterpieces Art Auction closes at 10.00pm on Monday 29 June. To arrange a viewing of the exhibition, please email es@eastbourne-college.co.uk or call 01323 452316 between 9.00am and 5.00pm, Monday to Friday. We look forward to welcoming you to Masterpieces and thank everyone who has contributed artwork, time and support to make this year’s exhibition possible.

Headmaster’s Welcome
A warm welcome to St Andrew’s – a dynamic, innovative prep school where we prepare our pupils for the fast pace and ever changing 21st century while maintaining the finest of prep school traditions.
Childhood is precious and the St Andrew’s Prep staff is committed to giving each of the children the happiest of starts in a warm and friendly environment while helping them to develop their individual strengths and characters.
We provide a firm academic grounding across our broad curriculum and ensure that every lesson and learning opportunity stimulates, encourages and engages the children. We believe lessons learned in the classroom are as important as those learned outside – on the sports field, at the beach or woodlands classroom, on the stage, on school trips, or in the boarding house.
Pastoral care, pupil wellbeing and happiness are at the heart of everything we do; and the children are at the centre of all our decision-making because, quite simply, we believe happy, healthy children thrive and achieve.
This website will give you a glimpse of the education, opportunities and positive challenges that a St Andrew’s Prep education will offer your child. Please enjoy exploring its pages and I hope it will whet your appetite for a visit during which, I’m sure, you’ll gain a real sense of the energy, enthusiasm, happiness and engagement of our children. I’m sure too you will see why we are so proud of the school’s heritage, location, facilities and staff but, most of all, the children who define us and are the school’s heartbeat.
I very much look forward to meeting you and your children at St Andrew’s Prep.

Meet the Headmaster – TOM GREGORY
Tom started his career in the City of London working in Investment Banking. After ten years he followed his heart and moved into teaching, immediately finding his vocation. He has held senior roles in various schools over the last sixteen years including Vinehall and Ashfold School where he was the Deputy Head.
St Andrew’s Prep and Eastbourne are familiar territory for Tom. As a former pupil at both St Andrew’s Prep and Eastbourne College, he knows first-hand the schools’ sense of family and community.
Tom is married to Esther, who is a career teacher in both senior and prep schools and they have two children, Maisie and Herbie.

Scholarships and Bursaries
Recognising and supporting excellence.
Scholarships
Scholarships are awarded to children who show outstanding potential in Academics, Art, Drama, Performing Arts, Music or Sport. We offer a tailored programme of provision and support for scholars to enhance, develop and inspire their particular area of talent.
Scholarships are prestigious awards and carry with them privilege and responsibility. The example scholars set will make them natural leaders among their peer group and we hope that they will both enjoy and make the most of the opportunity. Therefore, scholarships are awarded following a strictly moderated open competition.
Assessments are held each Lent Term and are available to external and internal candidates. Scholarships awarded to successful candidates will commence in the Michaelmas Term following the Lent Term assessments.
SCHOLARSHIP DATES
Application deadline
Bursaries
St Andrew’s Prep is committed to extending access to the school. We offer means-tested financial support to a number of pupils each year. These bursaries are separate from scholarships. Bursaries are offered in recognition of financial need.
The amount of a bursary award is calculated individually and the maximum offered is unlikely to exceed 50 percent. If a joint scholarship and bursary is awarded, then the amount of the scholarship is usually subsumed within the bursary and these combined awards are unlikely to exceed 50 percent.
All bursaries are means-tested and parents are asked to complete a comprehensive financial circumstances form which should be submitted to the Finance Bursar. Bursaries are set according to the guidelines laid down by the Independent Schools’ Bursars’ Association and are processed by our partner, Bursary Administration Limited, who will conduct a meeting with the parents to gain full understanding of the financial circumstances of the family.
For useful information about the scholarship and bursary process including important dates and application form, please contact the Registrar on 01323 733203 or email: admissions@standrewsprep.co.uk.
The closing date for all 2027 applications is Monday 11 January 2027 and scholarship assessments will take place later in the month.

Shape of the School Day
St Andrew’s Prep, Eastbourne offers a full and exciting timetable of lessons, activities and sports every weekday, with optional enrichment activities for pupils in Years 4 to 8 on Saturdays. As children progress through St Andrew’s Prep, slightly longer days allow them to explore a wider range of opportunities and prepare for smooth transitions through Pre-Prep, Juniors, Middles and Seniors, and ultimately on to their senior school education.
Our independent prep school in Eastbourne, East Sussex, located near the South Downs and the beautiful Eastbourne coastline, provides a strong focus on academic excellence, sports development and holistic education. At St Andrew’s Prep, Juniors (Years 3 & 4) take part in sports fixtures on alternate Thursday afternoons, while pupils in Years 5 to 8 enjoy competitive fixtures on Wednesday afternoons. Occasional Saturday sports fixtures also take place throughout the year, giving children the chance to develop teamwork, resilience, and confidence.
If you’re searching for a private prep school in East Sussex, discover why families choose St Andrew’s Prep, Eastbourne for its outstanding academics, enriching activities, and beautiful coastal location. We invite you to download our prospectus or book a visit today and experience the welcoming community at St Andrew’s Prep, Eastbourne.

Nursery Welcome
Nurturing curious, playful, happy children
St Andrew’s Prep Nursery in Eastbourne is a warm, welcoming early years setting for children aged 9 months to Pre-School age.
Based in Meads, Eastbourne, just a short stroll from the sea, the Nursery sits within our wider St Andrew’s Prep school community, often recognised among the best prep schools in Eastbourne and trusted by families across the local area.
Light, airy and homely, St Andrew’s Prep Nursery offers a nurturing environment that helps children become happy and confident children.
Located in two purpose-built buildings, the Lodge Nursery and the Casson Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Hub create a friendly and secure atmosphere within the school’s spacious grounds. We aim to give children the best possible educational start by providing a setting with no division between learning and play.
Being part of the wider St Andrew’s Prep school means that the Nursery enjoys many of the Pre-Prep and Prep facilities, including a state-of-the‑art sports hall and dance studio, gym, beautiful pavilion, resource centre, Woodland Classroom and extensive playing fields. As the school is located so close to the sea, the Nursery staff often take the children to the Eastbourne seafront to explore the beach and local area.
Families from Meads, Old Town, Upperton, Holywell and across Eastbourne choose St Andrew’s Prep Nursery for its safe, nurturing atmosphere and its beautiful balance of indoor and outdoor learning.
The Nursery is open 50 weeks of the year, from 8am to 6pm, offering wraparound care that fits the rhythm of modern family life. Children can join at any point during the year, making transitions smooth and stress‑free.
The Nursery is split into three classes – according to their age group.
For many parents whose older children are already at St Andrew’s Prep, the Nursery provides an ideal introduction for a younger sibling in friendly and familiar surroundings. Every child has a Key Person who is the main point of contact for parents. The Key Person builds a relationship with the child and their family, working together to ensure the best possible outcomes for their education and well-being.
Nursery children progress to the Reception class at St Andrew’s Prep or to other Eastbourne primary schools in the September after their fourth birthday, completing the Early Years Foundation Stage.
To find out more about St Andrew’s Prep Nursery in Eastbourne, please contact us. Call 01323 744820 for Admissions or click the button below to email us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative Arts and Sport at Pre Prep - St Andrew's Prep
pageCache.text:
Creative Arts and Sport at Pre Prep
Developing the whole child at Creative Arts and Sport at Pre Prep
At St Andrew’s Prep we recognise the importance of developing the whole child. This means balancing an academic curriculum with nurturing while enhancing children’s creativity and their physical abilities and skills.
Each week the children have PE and Games lessons, taught by specialist teachers. In Games lessons the children develop their competence in fundamental skills such as Agility, Hand-Eye Coordination, Reaction and Ball Handling Skills. Through progressive practices the children start to look at specific skills necessary for playing netball, football, rugby, hockey, cricket and tennis. They learn of teamwork skills and the basics of spatial awareness needed in invasion games. In PE lessons the children have the opportunity to develop their core strength, balance and movement skills for Gymnastics and Athletics.
The children also have a weekly swimming lesson, held in our indoor heated pool. The specialist teacher aims to build water confidence and work on basic stroke development.
Music and drama are also an important part of the school curriculum. Pre-Prep children have two or three music lessons a week, where, as well as learning a huge variety of songs and hymns, they learn how to compose music and about music theory. From Year 2 the children may learn a musical instrument, including piano, violin and cello; the discipline of playing an instrument greatly improves a child’s concentration, co-ordination and memory skills. The children also learn the art of performance, whether it be in their Nativities at Christmas, concerts during the year for Harvest, Spring and Summer or class assemblies. Year 2 are offered the possibility of LAMDA lessons to improve their confidence and performance skills. It is very important to learn Creative Arts and Sport at Pre Prep level.
Each academic year ends with celebrations of the children’s achievements in these areas. Parents are welcome to attend these events, including dance demonstrations, swimming galas and a Summer concert followed by Sports Day. During the latter, there is a great mix of competitive races and an inclusive pentathlon to ensure all children have opportunities to flourish. We encourage all parents to join in a race and show their child that sport is for all.

pageCache.text:
Friends of St Andrew’s
A role for parents at the heart of our community
All our parents are Friends of St Andrew’s. A group of parents and staff meet on a regular basis to form the Friends of St Andrew’s Committee and parents on the Committee act as representatives for their respective year groups. However, there are also opportunities to be a Friend of St Andrew’s and just ‘help’ and be ‘hands on deck’ for events without having to attend all the committee meetings.
Liaison with parents, staff and the wider community
Friends of St Andrew’s members act as a point of contact for the other parents in their year groups. In particular, they provide a warm welcome to parents who are new to the school. They also liaise with staff, present and past pupils and local residents and businesses. They play an important role within the life of the school and within the local community.
If you are interested in becoming a Friend of St Andrew’s or wish to contact us, please email us FOSA
Events
The Friends of St Andrew’s organise events throughout the school year and also support the school events by helping at these. These range from social gatherings for parents and fun events for the children, to fundraising events benefiting either local charities or special projects designed to enhance the children’s education and all-round experience at the school.
Events organised include some large annual events, such as Bonfire Night, the Advent Fayre, May Fayre, Colour Run and Summer Fayre, as well as other bi-annual events such as Burns Night and a Summer Ball. Smaller offerings are coffee mornings, quiz nights and cake sales, as well as serving refreshments at things like the Back to School and End of School Tea Parties.
The year group representatives also arrange informal get-togethers from time to time for the parents in their year groups.
Fundraising
In addition to raising funds for local charities, the Friends of St Andrew’s also raise money for and towards extra school projects. Recent examples include donating a new play area for the Middles, bench coats and floodlights for the sports department, large donation towards a new grand piano for the whole school, didi cars for breaktime enjoyment, an eco bird feed camera, bulbs for the whole school to plant and a glass wall to make the fives court more open for viewing.

Pastoral Care
nurturing happy, confident children
We take the responsibility of caring for all our children extremely seriously. We work to ensure there is a nurturing atmosphere in which each child feels cared for and important. This is achieved both formally through our Pastoral system and informally through the positive relationships the children are encouraged to build with each other and all the adults at the school.
Our Wellbeing Vision
Our wellbeing is fundamental to being well. It is a shared responsibility to look after each other, to offer support and to speak out. We see wellbeing as integral to the culture we promote; a constant thread and not an add-on.
Everyone deserves to feel safe, to be happy and to be as successful as they can be in all that they do. Looking after ourselves and being encouraged to do so proactively, will help us look after each other. With the support of friends, colleagues, home, and the whole pastoral care team everyone should know they are valued and celebrated for who they are. Mental health affects everyone in the same way as our physical health.
Our core values, our seaside location, our breadth of curriculum, our spiritual provision and our drive to raise awareness of challenges we might face will help make our community stronger and healthier.
Nursery
The St Andrew’s Prep Nursery boasts a team of qualified and experienced Nursery staff who are passionate and hold the strong belief that each child is unique and capable of great achievements. We have a holistic approach and provide enriching activities for all age groups allowing every child to be curious, explore, discover and take risks in a safe environment. We work to ensure that there is a nurturing atmosphere in which each child feels safe, cared for and important. This is achieved through our Pastoral Care and the positive relationships the children are helped to build with each other and all the adults at the school.
Every child within the Nursery is allocated a Key Person. The Key Person Approach promotes a reciprocal relationship between the member of staff, the child and their family. This provides the child with a sense of security so that they feel confident to explore their world and form further relationships. The role of the Key Person is to know a child and to support their sense of identity and individuality. They need to be aware of their individual child’s and family’s needs, preferences and development. Key Persons are also responsible for the planning and assessment of their children. During weekly staff meetings, any pastoral matters that may arise concerning children are shared between staff, ensuring the individual children’s needs are met. This information is shared with parents on a regular basis.
Staff believe that each child should have a ‘voice’. The children are encouraged and given opportunities to express themselves with confidence individually, as well as in a group.
Pre-Prep
We strive to ensure that children are happy, supported in their learning and sufficiently challenged by their work. Children are encouraged and helped to give of their best within a structured framework of friendly discipline. The focal person for each child and parent is the Class Teacher who teaches the children most subjects and also takes the leading pastoral role. Class Teachers work closely with the Head of Department to ensure children’s wellbeing is monitored.
The St Andrew’s key core values are followed in the Pre-Prep, as they are in the rest of the school. To positively encourage the keeping of the three core values, kindness, honesty and excellence, the Pre-Prep department awards patches during the weekly Celebration Assembly. The children are given these in the colour of their House set, to engender a sense of being part of a team and they are added to the display board situated in the Close Hall. We use Privilege Time to support our rewards and sanctions strategy.
Within the timetable there is time allocated for ‘Circle Time’ where the children engage in whole class discussion about positive and negative feelings and how the actions of others affect their own emotions. We also follow the Jigsaw programme of study to further develop an understanding of themselves and their relationships with others, during the PSHE lessons.
Prep
Pastoral Care at St Andrew’s is pro-active rather than reactionary and every child is cared for. The Head of Pastoral Care oversees the school’s Pastoral Leadership, which prioritises the wellbeing of every child.
The Pastoral Leadership Team includes the Deputy Head; Heads of Pre Prep, Juniors, Middles and Seniors; Head of Boarding; Head of Wellbeing; Head of Learning Support; School Counsellor and School Nurse who look strategically at Pastoral Care across the whole school, as well as meeting to discuss pupils.
Children in Years 3 and 4, who make up the Junior Department, continue to have a Class Teacher in a similar fashion to the Pre-Prep and that Class Teacher, with the support of the Head of Juniors, will take principal responsibility for the pastoral care of their children. From Year 5, children are looked after by their Form Tutor. The tutor system forms a vital link between the family and the school. The role of the Form Tutor is to encourage their tutees in academic and pastoral matters, so parents can be confident that there is a dedicated adult who takes a personal interest in their child’s wellbeing. Form Teachers and Tutors are readily available to talk to you about any aspects of school life.
Years 5 and 6 are called the Middles and Years 7 and 8 are called the Seniors. Each area is looked after by a Head of Section who champions pastoral care in those year groups. Assemblies are held for each area of the school as well as for the whole school to celebrate success, address pastoral issues and also to remind pupils of the school’s values.
Heads of Department coordinate their teams of tutors and feed in to the Head of Pastoral Care who oversees the school’s tutoring provision. This process is augmented through a comprehensive PSHE scheme of work. With growing social pressures on young people, we re-launched the SAPCA programme as a way of educating the children how to form opinions properly, how to substantiate ideas, how to self-reflect without over-analysing, how to listen and value other opinions, how to think critically and how to be aware of the wider community. In other words, we want to expand the minds of every pupil so that they become more resilient, more compassionate and better listeners.
Ultimately, the happiness of every child is crucial to the success of the pastoral care at St Andrew’s.
Since covid a new wellbeing hub has been opened called The Snug. This is a place where a child can come and be accepted just as they are at that moment, how they are feeling can be explored through play, talk or pictures and art.
The school listening service involves various members of staff who have all trained together in listening skills, offering appointments to children to come and talk in the Snug about absolutely anything. This has offered choice to the children (they can choose the teacher they would feel most comfortable to talk to), promoted staff development and also created a listening culture across the school. This has in turn promoted safeguarding and aided wellbeing for children and teachers too.
The culture of listening has really grown at St Andrews. Children will never be told to stop telling tales. Instead they are encouraged to speak with a teacher about anything on their minds. They will be listened to and helped to find solutions themselves, supported by the staff member. The Snug always has a sense of peace and calm about it and has been welcomed by staff and children alike.
St Andrew’s has built a Memory Garden for the purpose of encouraging children to remember people who they have loved and have died. Each year we hold a service specially to remember those people in the school community who have died. This has become an important part of the year and has provided comfort and support for some of our bereaved children and their families. This year we will be making time and space during the service to recognise the loss and grief that has been a reality for many in our society during the pandemic.
Other wellbeing highlights at St Andrew’s include Beach School and Woodland Classroom which enable our children to really make the most of the benefits of the outdoors. With the beach just moments away the Juniors have weekly planned sessions down on the beach and they could be doing anything from building imaginary creatures with the treasures that the latest tide has left behind and creating stories about them to investigating and identifying different types of seaweed. Whatever the activity it is always finished off with a cup of hot chocolate and a biscuit as we think about and admire each other’s creations and achievements. Teachers have undergone specialist training in Beach and Woodland Classroom. Both these can really benefit children’s wellbeing as they encourage enjoyment of being together, collaboration skills and an appreciation of natural beauty and the powerful forces of nature. Children who find it difficult to maintain focus in the classroom are often the ones who shine during outdoors education, revealing for example, great leadership qualities in a collaborative task or amazing imaginative writing skills when using the outdoors and nature as an inspiration for poetry writing.

Safeguarding
Eastbourne College and St Andrew’s Prep are part of the same Charity and share a commitment to providing a safe, supportive and nurturing environment for every child. Throughout this page, references to “the Charity” relate to both schools and reflect our shared approach to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.
Safeguarding is fundamental to everything we do across the Charity. We are committed to providing an environment in which children feel safe, supported and able to realise their full potential.
Creating and maintaining a safe environment is a shared responsibility. Everyone connected with the Charity, including staff, volunteers, governors, parents, families and pupils, has a role to play in promoting children’s wellbeing and protecting them from harm.
We take a whole-Charity approach to safeguarding, embedding it in our culture, policies and everyday practice. This helps ensure that the welfare of children remains central to every decision we make and every action we take. We have clear processes for raising concerns and are committed to ensuring that every concern is listened to, taken seriously and responded to appropriately. Further information can be found in our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.
How to raise a concern or seek advice?
We are committed to ensuring that all safeguarding concerns are handled promptly, appropriately and in line with our safeguarding procedures. Whether you are a pupil, parent, member of staff or visitor – we encourage you to raise any concerns you may have. The guidance below will help ensure your concern is directed to the most appropriate person.
Concern about the safety or wellbeing of a child
Please contact a member of the Safeguarding Team using the details below:
Mark Tomsett Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and Head of Pastoral Care mtomsett@standrewsprep.co.uk
Sarah Piper Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead and Head of Wellbeing spiper@standrewsprep.co.uk
Concern about the conduct of a member of staff
Please contact Mr Tom Gregory, Headmaster at St Andrew’s Prep tbgregory@standrewsprep.co.uk
Concern relating to the Headmaster, whistleblowing or general concerns about safeguarding practice
Please write to the Chair of Governors using the following address:
The Clerk to the Board of Governors Eastbourne College Marlborough House Old Wish Road Eastbourne East Sussex BN21 4JY
Full details of the Charity’s procedures for managing safeguarding concerns, allegations and whistleblowing can be found in our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.
Governance and oversight
The Board of Governors plays a vital role in ensuring that safeguarding remains a priority across the Charity. Working closely with school leaders and safeguarding teams, the Board provides oversight and assurance to ensure that effective safeguarding arrangements are in place and that the welfare of every child is protected.
Governors are responsible for ensuring that the Charity meets its safeguarding obligations and maintains the highest standards of care. This includes overseeing safeguarding policies and procedures, monitoring compliance with statutory requirements, supporting safe recruitment practices and ensuring that staff receive appropriate safeguarding training.
Through regular review and scrutiny, the Board helps to ensure that safeguarding is embedded in the Charity’s decision-making, policies and day-to-day practice.
If you wish to contact the Chair of Governors regarding a safeguarding matter, please write to:
The Clerk to the Board of Governors Eastbourne College Marlborough House Old Wish Road Eastbourne East Sussex BN21 4JY
Further information about the Charity’s governance arrangements, including details of all Governors, can be found on our Governors page.
Policies and guidance
Our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy sets out the Charity’s approach to keeping children safe and promoting their welfare.
Further policies relating to safeguarding, pupil welfare and the wider operation of the Charity can be found in our Policies section. The Policies section also includes links to our most recent and previous ISI Inspection Reports.
To learn more about how we support the wellbeing, development and care of our pupils, please visit our Pastoral Care page.

What our parents say
Don’t just take our word for it… below is a collection of just some of the many testimonials we receive on a regular basis. Our strongest advocates are our parents and our excellent reputation spreads by word of mouth.
“I have children with different needs across the academic, sporting, and musical curriculum. St Andrew’s Prep has met all these needs from behavioural issues to nurturing academic talent. While my husband and I are busy working, I am also impressed with how much we get back if we participate in the whole experience the school offers. I genuinely feel my children and I are better versions of ourselves not just because of the facilities and talented staff but also the purpose and community St Andrew’s embodies for us.” Parent of children in Year 2 and Year 4
“Having been a parent at the school for nearly 20 years I have been lucky enough to experience many updates and refurbishments to St Andrew’s. With our son’s journey starting there and culminating with a first-class honours degree, the strong foundations were laid at St Andrew’s. I feel that the school offers an all-round education that was continued and enhanced through his journey at Eastbourne College. Our daughter is now at St Andrew’s and with a new sports hall and investment in the performing arts department we hope the school continues to grow and our daughter benefits from this all-round education.” Parent of children through the school for the last 20 years
“Our son started his life at St Andrew’s at 8 months old when he joined the wonderful nursery. Over the last 5 years I have watched him bloom under the loving kind attention of all the staff at the school. We truly feel the school is a part of our family and it’s a wonderful feeling to know we have this group to be part of our lives.” Parent of a child in Reception
